title: Movement in the rule
hook: a daily walk or stretch: Cook Ding's knife followed the natural lines, and his lord learned from it how to nourish life
tomorrow: why does the Torah say to bless God after the meal, not before?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: sleep first. Jesus slept in the stern after a full day, storm or no storm. Today the body gets up and moves.

The sound comes first: a soft rip, a slice, a steady rhythm. In the kitchen of a lord named Wen Hui, a cook named Ding is cutting up an ox. Every move of his hand, his shoulder, his foot, his knee falls in time, like a dance to old court music. The lord stands watching and can hardly believe it. Ah, he says, how can skill go this far? The cook lays down his knife. What I love, he says, is the Way, and it goes beyond skill.
screen: `A RIP, A SLICE, A RHYTHM.` → `COOK DING AT WORK.` → `HAND, SHOULDER, FOOT, KNEE, IN TIME.` → `WHAT I LOVE IS THE WAY.`

segments.voice: This story is from the Zhuangzi, a classic book of Taoism. Ding explains. When he started, all he could see was the whole ox. After three years, he no longer saw it whole. Now he meets it with his spirit, not his eyes, and follows the natural lines: the blade slides through the gaps at the joints and never strikes bone. A good cook, he says, changes his knife every year, because he cuts. An ordinary cook changes it every month, because he hacks. Ding's knife has lasted nineteen years and is as sharp as the day it left the whetstone. And when he comes to a hard knot, he slows down, watches closely, moves his hand gently, and it comes apart. Then the lord says the line the chapter is named for: from my cook's words, I have learned how to nourish life. Here's the teaching. In Taoism, nourishing life means caring for the body by following its grain, not forcing it. Later Taoists, tradition says, used the same words for gentle daily practices of movement and breath. That's the measure for movement in your rule. Not a punishment you hack through until something gives. A daily walk or stretch that follows the lines your body actually has, slows down at the hard knots, and keeps you sharp for years.
screen: `HE FOLLOWS THE NATURAL LINES.` · `THE GOOD COOK CUTS; THE ORDINARY ONE HACKS.` · `SLOW AT THE HARD KNOT.` · `I HAVE LEARNED TO NOURISH LIFE.` · then, large: `MOVE DAILY.`

segments.voice: Stand up, if you can, and stretch slowly: arms overhead, then a gentle twist, then a reach toward the floor. Go only as far as the body opens easily, like Ding's knife finding the gaps. Where something is tight, slow down and breathe there, and keep moving gently through the sit.
Movement in the rule: a daily walk or stretch written into your rule, following your body's grain, the way Cook Ding's knife followed the natural lines.
Your line: move daily. Cook Ding's knife followed the lines and stayed sharp for years. Day 1646, on your feet.

screen: `DAY 1646 COUNTS.` → `THE BODY · 2 OF 8.` → `TOMORROW: WHY DOES THE TORAH SAY TO BLESS GOD AFTER THE MEAL, NOT BEFORE?`

howItsDone: Taoist teachers speak of nourishing life, yangsheng, and keep gentle daily movement and breath under that name. On a personal rule, movement can be a daily walk or stretch at a set time.

Zhuangzi.meaning: a classic Taoist book of stories, named for the thinker it's credited to

Cook Ding.meaning: the cook in the Zhuangzi whose knife never dulls

Wen Hui.meaning: the lord who watched Cook Ding at work

the Way.meaning: the Tao: the way things naturally go, in Taoist teaching

Taoism.meaning: a Chinese tradition of living in harmony with the Way, the Tao
